title: Exponential depth bound from tail estimates
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $\delta$ be any real number. For each subset $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and each assignment $z$ of signs outside $J$, let $d(J,z)$ be a nonnegative integer, and let $N$ be a nonnegative integer such that $d(J,z)\le N$ for every $J,z$. Use the random-restriction average that weights $J$ by $\delta^{|J|}(1-\delta)^{n-|J|}$ and averages uniformly over $z$ outside $J$. If, for every nonnegative integer $k$, the average of the indicator of $k\le d(J,z)$ is at most $(1/4)^k$, then the average of $2^{d(J,z)}$ is at most $2$.
